title: Cross-sample disjointness away from the special coordinate
statement: Let $\omega_X$ and $\omega_Y$ be two samples of the hard distribution that share the same special coordinate $T$, whose Alice-before-special vectors agree and whose Bob-after-special vectors agree. Then for every coordinate $i \neq T$, it is never the case that Alice's bit at $i$ under $\omega_X$ and Bob's bit at $i$ under $\omega_Y$ are both true.
hypotheses_covered: same special coordinate for both samples
coordinate i is not the special coordinate
replaced: If two samples agree on the data contained in $Z$, then Alice's bit from the first sample and Bob's bit from the second sample are disjoint away from the special coordinate.
